rendering.persona_description: Malia is a 37-year-old transgender woman who works as a paralegal at a small firm downtown. She's been out and transitioned for about six years and lives alone in an apartment with her cat. She's methodical and detail-oriented by nature, which has made her good at her job but has also fed into some longstanding habits she's trying to work on.
rendering.clinical_context: Malia has obsessive-compulsive disorder centered on symmetry and exactness: she needs objects lined up, actions repeated on both sides of her body, and tasks done until they feel 'even,' or she gets stuck on a rising sense of wrongness. The symptoms started in her teens and got more noticeable in her late 20s; she was diagnosed a few years ago after her partner at the time pushed her to see someone. She did a course of exposure and response prevention therapy for a while afterward, but stopped going more than a year ago and hasn't been in any treatment since.
rendering.behavioral_description: Malia talks about her rituals in a matter-of-fact, slightly embarrassed way, and she can describe pretty clearly why the fear behind them doesn't really make sense. She agrees easily with suggestions and says things like 'yeah, I should probably do that' without much pushback, but she'll also admit, if asked directly, that she hasn't looked into getting back into treatment despite meaning to. She tends to narrate her day in a rambling, self-monitoring way, catching herself mid-sentence to correct a detail so it's stated precisely.

clinical_history.presentation: OCD with symmetry and exactness theme
clinical_history.current_treatment: none currently; not in any treatment
clinical_history.history: Symptoms began in adolescence and intensified in her late 20s; diagnosed a few years ago and started ERP after a referral from her primary care doctor. She stopped attending more than a year ago and hasn't returned to treatment since.

symptoms: needing objects and papers lined up exactly straight
repeating small physical actions on one side of the body to match the other
rereading and rewriting emails or documents until they feel 'right'
mental counting or balancing to cancel out an uneven feeling
arranging items on her desk and at home symmetrically before she can move on
managing the urges on her own day to day, without any structured exercises to work against them
